bibliography.title: Simultaneous Speech-to-Speech Translation Without Aligned Data

sections.title: 3.2 Coarse alignment of speech translation data
Conflict of interest and Impact Statement

abstract_sentences.text: Simultaneous speech translation requires translating source speech into a target language in real-time while handling non-monotonic word dependencies.

Traditional approaches rely on supervised training with word-level aligned data, which is difficult to collect at scale and thus depends on synthetic alignments using language-specific heuristics that are suboptimal.
We propose Hibiki-Zero, which eliminates the need for word-level alignments entirely.

evidence.anchor: eliminates the need for word-level alignments entirely

abstract_sentences.text: This fundamentally simplifies the training pipeline and enables seamless scaling to diverse languages with varying grammatical structures, removing the bottleneck of designing language-specific alignment heuristics.

We first train on sentence-level aligned data to learn speech translation at high latency, then apply a novel reinforcement learning strategy using GRPO to optimize latency while preserving translation quality.

evidence.anchor: optimize latency while preserving translation quality

abstract_sentences.text: Hibiki-Zero achieves state-of-the-art performance in translation accuracy, latency, voice transfer, and naturalness across four X-to-English tasks.
Moreover, we demonstrate that our model can be adapted to support a new input language with less than 1000h of speech.
We provide examples, model weights, inference code and we release a benchmark containing 45h of multilingual data for speech translation evaluation.

final_judgment.single_storyline: Sentence-level coarse alignment trains a high-latency multistream S2ST/S2TT base, then BLEU-only prefix process rewards and GRPO learn the simultaneous listen/speak policy (pp.2–5, §§3.2–3.3; pp.6–9, §4).
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The body keeps token information flow, Eq.1–8, training budgets, Tables 1–3 and α/n_w/alignment ablations, preserving decisions about quality, latency and adaptation (pp.3–9).
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Appendix moves base-stage comparisons, training curves, Italian retention and four-language α examples to pp.13–20; stage attribution and regression checks depend on it.
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 2's stream timing, Figure 3's prefix-BLEU reward, Tables 1–2's objective/human pairing and B/C's temporal failure diagnosis create the clearest evidence chain (pp.3,5–9).
final_judgment.largest_gap: The cross-language summary is stronger than some row-level Table 1 differences, and seeds, repeats, hardware and uncertainty definitions are absent; synthetic TTS/Whisper evaluation also limits external validity (pp.6–9).
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For real-time generation, use a scoreable intermediate sequence and sentence-level reference to provide local credit assignment while retaining an outcome-quality signal, then evaluate the same loop with explicit latency metrics (pp.4–5, Eq.3–8).
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This applies when intermediate outputs, references and latency metrics exist; it does not establish RL convergence, real interpretation safety, arbitrary target-language generalization or inference-time trade-off control (p.9, §4.8).
